purpose: Teach: せっせと/おっちゃん/大方/易く/総じて/ひそか/カワイイ/凄まじい

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがせっせと田んぼを耕されたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father worked the rice paddies so tirelessly.
lines.style: Soft, distant recall. Voice settles on the image of his father's hands in mud. Slow, steady rhythm—almost measuring time in strokes of work. Gentle conviction underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、近所のおっちゃんと将棋を指されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather played shogi with the neighbors all the time, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm interjection, eyes bright with her own memory. Quick and affectionate on 'dear'—a small pull back into the present, teasing gently. She's not correcting him; she's adding her own layer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは大方の不満を口にされなかった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father rarely complained—no matter what troubled him.
lines.style: Quieter now, almost a confession. The weight of unsaid things in the pause before 'rarely.' A slight furrow in the delivery—he's reaching for something he couldn't name then. Respectful distance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、書道を易く教えて下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather taught calligraphy so patiently, didn't he, dear? Even to clumsy hands like mine.
lines.style: A small laugh threaded through. Pride without boasting. She's defending the memory—softening what he's building toward. Affectionate, patient tone, like she's gentling a horse.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんは総じて寡黙な方でらした
lines.en: Gran, your father was a quiet man—that's what I remember most. Quiet all the way through.
lines.style: A long exhale here. The word 'quiet' carries the weight of decades. He's not judging; he's bearing witness. Voice slows on 'all the way through'—like setting something down carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様にひそかにお小遣いを渡されてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he'd slip money to the grandchildren when he thought no one was looking, remember? He was kind that way.
lines.style: A knowing smile in the voice. She's weaving tenderness through his sorrow—gently insisting on the whole picture. Warm, conspiratorial, like they're sharing a secret together still.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お孫様の事を「カワイイ」と仰ってたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, he called the grandchildren 'cute'—I remember that. He said it like he meant it.
lines.style: A rare softness breaks through. The memory of his father saying one simple, unguarded thing. Voice opens here—less wistful, more vulnerable. Almost surprised by his own tenderness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦時下の凄まじい体験をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather lived through terrible things in the war, didn't he, dear? Things he carried quietly.
lines.style: Her voice lowers, becomes steadier. She's honoring what he carried without asking him to say it aloud. Close, intimate—the voice of someone who knows his weight and holds it with him.
